title: Does network topology shape faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi? — matched-density scale-free hub vs distributed ring; structure (cut-resistance) not edge-count governs integration
question: At matched edge count, does a scale-free hub network integrate more (faithful big-Phi) than a distributed ring under parity dynamics?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib (reused, NOT reinvented): iit4_bigphi.big_phi + iit4_bit/iit4_pow2 (via stdlib/consciousness/*). network->TPM bridge (net_tpm, parity/XOR-of-neighbours) generalises eca_tpm to an arbitrary graph; inlined in the harness.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
toolchain_note: built via fix-1180 bypass: HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 HEXA_LANG=<root> hexa.real.bak-2026-05-22-pre-no-hxc build <src> -o <bin>. See reference-life-cycle-hexa-run-gotchas.
dynamics: parity: TPM[s*n+i] = (sum_{j in N(i)} bit_j(s)) mod 2
metric_def: Phi_mean = mean over all 2^n states of big_phi(tpm, n, st)[0] (n=4 exact).

RING_4cycle.note: matched density yet Phi=0 — see confound

verdict_class: H1 SUPPORTED (with confound, see honest_limits L1)
finding: At matched edge count (4 edges) a scale-free hub network integrates far more (faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi_mean=6.81) than a distributed 4-cycle (0.0) under parity dynamics — topology, NOT edge-count, governs integration (EMPTY 0 -> SF 6.81 > K4 5.625 is also non-monotone in density). HONEST CONFOUND (L1): the 4-cycle's Phi=0 is largely a parity-even-cycle bipartite-decoupling artifact (node0==node2 update b1^b3, node1==node3 update b0^b2 -> redundant nodes / linear reducible), so the magnitude over-favours the hub, AND a regular cycle is NOT a random ER graph, so the literal 'scale-free > random ER' claim is only weakly probed. The robust takeaway is the WEAK form: topology (not density) determines Phi; hub integrates, even-cycle-parity is reducible. A clean ER-ensemble test needs n>=5 (Phi-engine cost; deferred).
honest_limits: L1 (CONFOUND, key): 4-cycle Phi=0 is largely a parity-even-cycle bipartite decoupling (node0==node2, node1==node3 updates -> reducible), not a pure topology effect; AND a cycle != a random ER graph. Literal 'scale-free > random ER' only weakly tested; robust claim is the weak form (topology not density governs Phi).
L2: parity is one dynamics; majority/threshold/non-linear may not have the even-cycle degeneracy -> RING Phi could be >0. Dynamics-robustness untested.

L3: n=4 small, one graph per class (not ensemble); at n=4 a 4-edge non-hub non-cycle graph is essentially absent -> topology variety limited. Clean ER-vs-SF ensemble needs n>=5 (n=5 big-Phi state-average = 128 calls, deferred for engine cost).
L4: Phi_mean averages a state-dependent quantity (FAITHFUL_REMEASURE 4) -> direction robust, magnitude state-dependent.
L5: parity networks are topology proxies, not brain/life networks; labels are graph-structure, not phenomenal claims.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi, not full-IIT4 absolute calibration; direction comparison robust to scale offset.
L7: verdict is a measurement fact on a toy network, NOT 'hub brains are more conscious'.

verify_fence.claim: H_289 at matched edge-count (4) a scale-free hub integrates far more (faithful IIT4 big-Phi_mean=6.81) than a distributed 4-cycle (0.0) under parity dynamics — topology not density governs integration; CONFOUND: the 4-cycle's zero is largely a parity-even-cycle bipartite-decoupling artifact and a cycle is not a random ER graph; deterministic toy-substrate outcome, NOT an atlas identity
verify_fence.reason: imagination/metaphor class (hexa-bio AXIS) — verification N/A by design; values deterministic arithmetic, interpretation fenced + confound-flagged
